mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation environment.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when labor market indicators are strong.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase above 0.4 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of high wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which compresses earnings for cyclically-sensitive sectors and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when commodity prices spike independently.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units for four consecutive months signals a sustained weakness in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong mortgage rate declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is impossible; however, a sharp drop in PAYEMS alongside a rise in UNRATE exceeding 0.3pp signals significant labor market churning and weakness, which reduces aggregate demand and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > -20,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals reduced household buffer capacity, which increases sensitivity to income shocks and amplifies recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rapid credit expansion.
